title: Effect on Retail Tenant Mix and Leasing Terms at The Clementi Mall Following Acquisition by Owner of Neighbouring Mall
what_it_is: Effect on Retail Tenant Mix and Leasing Terms at The Clementi Mall Following Acquisition by Owner of Neighbouring Mall

sections.label: Singapore voluntary merger notification regime
sections.summary: Singapore uses a voluntary merger notification regime to balance effective regulatory oversight with low compliance costs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: With regard to competition concerns arising from mergers and acquisitions, Singapore adopts a voluntary merger notification regime to balance between effective regulatory oversight and keeping compliance costs low.

sections.label: Clementi Mall acquisition notification
sections.summary: The parties to The Clementi Mall acquisition have not formally notified CCS, which will monitor developments and can step in.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The parties to the acquisition of The Clementi Mall have not formally notified CCS for a merger assessment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: CCS will continue to monitor market developments and is empowered to step in, if it obtains information suggesting that a merger may result in potential competition issues.

sections.label: Tenancy mix market driven
sections.summary: For commercial developments, the tenancy mix is primarily market driven and results from commercial decisions by owners, operators and tenants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: I want to thank the Member, Mr David Hoe, for his three comprehensive supplementary questions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: I think it bears repeating, for commercial developments, the tenancy mix is primarily market driven and a result of commercial decisions that is made by mall owners, operators as well as tenants.

sections.label: CCS assessment and intervention grounds
sections.summary: CCS assesses competition based on facts and circumstances, and will step in for substantially less competition or coordinated behaviour, with public feedback welcome.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: CCS will assess the degree to which competition may be affected or is affected, based on facts, based on circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Certainly, not based on hearsay, uncertainty, projections and so on.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: I want to assure the Member that, for example, if any transaction results in substantially less competition that compromises the consumer welfare, CCS will step in.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Another example is if CCS observes the behaviour of the organisations and if we pick up signals that they are coordinating the behaviour to raise prices, to reduce quality, to reduce output, to reduce innovation, CCS will step in.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: I want to assure the Member that members of the public, including his residents, can certainly provide feedback – qualitative as well as quantitative – to CCS directly.
